projects.title: ENI Network
projects.description: ENI is a modular Layer 1 blockchain built for mass commercial adoption, with a hub chain, app-chains and one-click chain launch. I was a UI/UX designer and frontend developer on the early team, and designed and built part of the site's pages, including the mobile versions of several of them.

story.label: The idea
story.text: Decisions made together. We worked it out together through wireframes and MVPs. Every design decision answered to two things: the client's requirements and the conventions of Web3.

story.label: Why this look
story.text: Serious infrastructure, Web3 language. ENI is a Layer 1 blockchain built for commercial adoption, so the site has to feel like serious infrastructure. It also speaks the visual language Web3 audiences recognise: a dark ground, neon-lit wireframe landscapes and 3D renders of the sentinel node hardware. The pages I worked on follow that system and the client's requirements, so they sit comfortably beside the rest of the site.

story.label: How it was built
story.text: Early team, first idea to version three. I was part of the early team, working with designers, a PM and developers. We worked together from the first ideas through to the third version of the build, before the project passed to another team.

projects.title: ASEAN Labs
projects.description: ASEAN Labs is a Web3 project incubator that helps teams build on ENI across Southeast Asia. I designed and built the site on my own, with custom vector illustrations drawn in Figma, a design system set up in code so every page stays consistent, and motion and micro-interactions throughout.

story.label: The problem
story.text: No professional landing page. Our team lacked a professional landing page to stand out in marketing and on social media. The site also needed to set out what the team offers, how it works with projects, and which projects belong to the ENI ecosystem.

story.label: The idea
story.text: Simple, agency-style structure. This is the website for my team, a Web3 project incubator. I kept the direction simple: 2D animated vector illustrations in solid colours, with each section structured like an agency website. The sections follow what a visitor needs to know, from the capabilities and the process to the ecosystem.

story.label: Why this look
story.text: A look that feels decisive. ASEAN Labs is an incubator whose promise is execution, so the site is built to look decisive. It has a solid yellow ground, black linework and flat vector illustrations, with no gradients or glow in the hero. Next to the dark neon pages many Web3 teams ship, it stands out in marketing and on social media, which was the gap the team had. Mono captions and a dot grid give it a builder's workshop feel, and agency-style sections keep it easy to scan.

story.label: How it was built
story.text: Built with AI and a design system. Once the team agreed with the design direction, I moved on to development with AI. With the right skill.md files and design instructions, the AI agent executed it well. MVPs settled the look before the build, and iteration tuned it after. Some of the vectors are custom made by me in Figma, and the logos were made by our team. A design system set up in code keeps every page consistent, with motion and micro-interactions throughout.

projects.title: Kairma
projects.description: Kairma deploys AI employees inside cross-border operations, keeping brand data local on a sealed, on-premise runtime. Kairma forward-deploys AI employees into the markets a brand enters and runs them to outcomes, so the business judges them by results instead of headcount. Each task is routed live across models such as Claude, GPT and Gemini, by task and cost, while the data stays inside a sealed runtime called the Keep. This was a solo project, so I designed the site and shipped it myself. Its model router section pulls the AI model rankings live from the OpenRouter API, ranked by daily usage.

story.label: The problem
story.text: A client unsure how to convey its message. The client wanted a unique landing page for their brand as an AI company, but was unsure how to convey the message about their business. The page had to explain what Kairma does: AI employees for cross-border operations, running on a sealed, on-premise runtime that keeps brand data local.

story.label: The idea
story.text: A myth-inspired direction. The client loved the mythical gods in the footer image, so I explored ideas within it and took a myth-inspired direction for the animated illustrations. I began by brainstorming with AI tools to play with the art and design style of the mythical gods the client preferred, gathering references from several sources, Pinterest among them. I then fed those references to AI agents for creative ideation, which kept the exploration loose until a direction was clear, and proceeded with isometric illustrations of tools and instruments inspired by the myth gods, one for each part of the platform. The page is structured so that every section uses its space with a clear purpose.

story.label: Why this look
story.text: Built around a vault. Kairma sells a sealed, on-premise runtime, so the page is built around a vault. The hero is the Keep drawn in isometric, a stone building with a pediment and columns that nods to the myth theme the client liked, with a key to pull and a readout showing raw data out at 0 B. Near-black, IBM Plex and one red accent, used on the Request a pilot button and on small details of the drawing, give it the sober tone an operations buyer expects from infrastructure. A light paper theme keeps the same layout and swaps the red for a deep green.

story.label: How it was built
story.text: System first, then the build. Before I build anything, I set up the system: the selected skills.md files and the design system. Then I lay out the user journey and the information architecture, and only after that move on to the content structure and development. For Kairma, specific skill.md files guided the AI that produced the animated illustrations, and the footer image was edited with a dither effect using an open-source website. Consultations and MVPs refined the UI/UX and technical decisions first, and once the client was satisfied with the MVP I moved on to the build with minimal iteration.

projects.title: Stashcube
projects.description: Stashcube is a curated library for AI-native designers and builders, in one searchable place. It gathers UI libraries, 3D tools, icons, fonts, inspiration and AI skills. I conceived, designed and built it end to end.

story.label: The problem
story.text: A growing collection to sort. AI-native designers and builders depend on a kit of libraries and templates. I began by keeping mine in Notion, but as the collection grew it needed a better way to sort and categorise it.

story.label: The idea
story.text: A library shared with the community. Stashcube started as a library of curated libraries for my own use. Most of them are open source, so I decided to share it with the community and the public. It now gathers over 200 links across 15 categories, from UI libraries and 3D tools to icons, fonts, inspiration and AI skills. Everything is sorted into categories, with a Recently added section for new finds and a My go-to stack section for my own picks.

story.label: Why this look
story.text: Near-black, content first. A moodboard of references came first. Stashcube is a library, so the interface stays near-black and neutral and lets the content lead, with one lime accent to show what to click. I chose a partial-pixel theme for the character: a pixel texture that fades out toward the edge nods to builder culture without covering anything. A left sidebar grouped under Build, Create and Brand lets visitors move through the collection like a file explorer.

projects.title: FlowFi
projects.description: FlowFi is decentralized infrastructure for the institutional management of on-chain capital, built on ENI. It runs two treasuries: a Governance Treasury that sets the rules and consensus, and an Investor Treasury that grows capital through deployment and incubation. Its FF token launches through the Black Hole Launch, a fair-launch distribution. I designed and built the landing page that sets out the protocol, its tokenomics and its roadmap.

story.label: The problem
story.text: A lot to explain on one page. The client needed a landing page that explains what FlowFi is, along with its tokenomics and roadmap. There is a lot to set out: two treasuries, and a fair-launch token distribution through the Black Hole Launch.

story.label: The idea
story.text: Showing the flow. FlowFi needed to show its flow, so I looked for inspiration that resonates with the brand. I wanted to portray the smoothness of the project and its tokenomics, and the on-scroll trigger animation fit best: its flowing motion blends naturally with the name and carries the business flow from end to end. I proposed that direction first, then polished it and adjusted it to the client's requests. The timeline was the challenge for me, so I found a reference component for it that suits FlowFi's branding too.

story.label: Why this look
story.text: Pale and open, not dark and neon. On-chain finance often defaults to dark and neon. FlowFi manages institutional capital, so the look is pale and open instead, with one purple accent and a confident display face, a tone that reads as calm and accountable rather than speculative. The logo's layered ribbons already suggest capital in motion, which is why the flowing on-scroll animation feels native to the brand.

story.label: How it was built
story.text: Custom illustrations that resonate with the brand. After discussing it with the client, we agreed on a clean isometric set of assets. Using Pinterest references, I made the isometric SVGs in Figma, customised with FlowFi's branding and logos. The sections follow a clear structure down the page, so the protocol, its tokenomics and its roadmap each have a place of their own.

projects.title: PayGo
projects.description: PayGo is an x402 payment gateway on ENI Mainnet that lets APIs and AI agents pay per request over plain HTTP. I designed and built the developer site on my own, put together from components of a UI library, with an interactive protocol walkthrough that explains the payment flow.

story.label: The problem
story.text: Payments built for machines. The site makes the case for machine-native payments. AI agents cannot solve CAPTCHAs or manage 2FA, and subscriptions do not suit sporadic, high-speed tasks, so an agent needs to pay exactly for what it uses.

story.label: The idea
story.text: An interactive protocol walkthrough. The client came with the idea and the direction. The payment flow is an interactive protocol walkthrough in three steps: the client sends a request, the server answers 402 Payment Required with a price, and the client pays and receives the resource.

story.label: Why this look
story.text: Speaking in developer materials. PayGo's audience is developers, so the site speaks in their materials. It has a dark ground, Inter for clarity, and JetBrains Mono for the curl and HTTP 402 snippets that make the walkthrough credible. The headline sets its last word, Settlements, in an italic serif, a small change of voice that marks where a request ends up. A violet tint gives a technical product some warmth.

story.label: How it was built
story.text: Refined with the client, then handed over. I consulted on and refined the UI/UX and technical decisions with the client. Once we agreed on the result, I handed the site over to the client's in-house team to run.

projects.title: OpenCrew
projects.description: OpenCrew is a talent marketplace and growth partner for Web3, AI and new finance projects. People can hire its global crew of executives, advisors, consultants, regional leaders and spokespersons, placed into real roles. Its client stories come from projects we incubated, its photos are real, taken at my own offline events, and its illustrations are custom SVGs drawn in Figma.

story.label: The idea
story.text: Talent recruiting, marketplace style. A side project for talent recruiting in the Web3 space. I built a marketplace-style site where people can hire our services, browse the crew, or join it. The site is still maintained after launch. The site shows real experience and on-site activity, with photos taken at my own offline events and client stories from projects we incubated. It also presents a talent pool with professional experiences, for clarity.

story.label: Why this look
story.text: Black and gold, premium first. OpenCrew places senior operators into real roles, so the first impression has to say premium before anyone reads a word. I proposed black and gold for that: a pure black ground, white type in a firm sans, and gold as a warm glow and the Contact button, so it reads as a signal rather than decoration. The team agreed with the direction.

projects.title: Fortuna HK
projects.description: Fortuna HK Holdings provides cross-border education, wealth management and corporate services. I designed and built the multilingual site on my own.

story.label: The problem
story.text: Two audiences, two sets of services. Fortuna HK serves individuals and companies, so the site separates personal services from corporate services. Personal services cover education and residency planning in Hong Kong, wealth and property, and healthcare. Corporate services cover company registration, government subsidies and capital operations.

story.label: The idea
story.text: A direction set by the client. The client set the design direction. I started by helping them choose a theme and mood that suit the business, then suggested and refined what the site needed, based on their requirements and the nature of the business.

story.label: Why this look
story.text: Restraint that builds trust. Fortuna advises on wealth, education and corporate structure, where trust comes from restraint. The theme is a charcoal ground, thin light type and one warm bronze accent, with a single sculpted object at the centre of the hero in place of stock photography. It signals premium and discretion, and gives the site one image visitors remember.

story.label: How it was built
story.text: Multilingual, with a world clock. The site is multilingual. The world clock in the footer was made at the client's request, and the imagery is AI-assisted.

projects.title: Nikola
projects.description: Nikola is an AI coordination layer for projects on ENI, covering AI governance, protocol design and capital. I designed and built the site on my own, with effects and shaders from a UI component library.

story.label: The problem
story.text: Three layers, one site. Nikola is built in three layers: an incubator, an AI governance agent and an on-chain DeFi protocol. Its product stack marks what is live and what is still in development, and the site is organised around infrastructure, products, ecosystem, governance and roadmap.

story.label: The idea
story.text: A direction the client agreed to. I helped the client choose a theme and mood that fit the business. I then set the design direction, and the client agreed to it.

story.label: Why this look
story.text: A hero made of light. Nikola is an AI coordination layer, an idea with nothing physical to show, so the hero is made of light. Streaks of violet, gold and blue cross a near-black field, like signals moving between nodes. A deep violet ground rather than flat black gives the dark theme a cooler, more technical tone, and Plus Jakarta Sans keeps the long architecture and governance sections easy to read.

story.label: How it was built
story.text: Straight from direction to build. The client's guidelines and documentation made the build straightforward. The work moved from the agreed direction straight to the build.

projects.title: PUSC
projects.description: PUSC is a DAO-governed, over-collateralised stablecoin protocol pegged 1:1 to USD. It is a microsite for PayGo. The client chose the theme and mood, and I built the site to match, with custom shaders and custom assets.

story.label: The problem
story.text: Shared mood, its own variation. PUSC is a microsite for PayGo, so it shares PayGo's mood and adds its own variation. The client chose the theme and mood, which left little to settle before the build.

story.label: The idea
story.text: Explaining the stablecoin. The page walks through how the stablecoin works. It covers a 1:1 USD peg, over-collateralised minting, DAO governance and a Blackhole burn that removes supply through transfer fees. Each principle is paired with a terminal-style readout.

story.label: Why this look
story.text: Money first, code second. A stablecoin has to look like money before it looks like code. So the hero is a minted coin with embossed lettering and a metallic finish in the page's own violet-blue. The code half is the terminal-style readouts beside each principle, which turn the algorithmic parts, the peg and the collateral ratio, into something a visitor can read at a glance. Sharing PayGo's dark violet mood makes the two sites feel like one family.

story.label: How it was built
story.text: Custom shaders and assets. The shaders and assets are custom made for the site. After the build, I handed it over.

events.title: Selangor AI & Semiconductor Summit 2026
events.description: I spoke on the Fire Stage at the Selangor AI & Semiconductor Summit 2026. While the programme centred on chips and infrastructure, my session addressed the human side: preparing everyday Malaysians for this shift. I presented the talent-building work of the MyDAC Malaysia and LEJIEND joint venture, which offers free community learning almost every week, online and in person at Outreach Coffee in Bukit Bintang.
events.conclusion: Infrastructure only delivers value when people are ready to use it, so preparing everyday Malaysians through regular, free learning is as much a part of the AI and semiconductor story as the chips themselves.

events.title: ENI DeFi Week World Tour
events.description: I spoke at ENI DeFi Week in Changsha, representing ASEAN Labs as the official project incubator for ENI. Organised by ENI, the event introduced the network and its ecosystem to Mainland Chinese audiences, and my session took the room through what is being built on ENI. ASEAN Labs helps Web3 teams build on ENI across Southeast Asia, and Changsha gave us a first-hand look at the China market for DeFi and Web3. Thank you to the ENI team for hosting us.
events.conclusion: Reaching the China market for DeFi and Web3 starts with a clear role in the ecosystem, and ASEAN Labs holds that role as the official project incubator for ENI.

events.title: Web3 + RWA Global Infrastructure Summit
events.description: I represented ASEAN Labs at the Web3 + RWA Global Infrastructure Summit in Hangzhou, organised by ENI. While the summit centred on Web3 and real-world assets, my session was about taking part: I introduced the MEX launchpad and the DAOaaS platform, where users can join as a community and farm for airdrops. It was a good place to show both to an audience following Web3 and real-world assets.
events.conclusion: Alongside a summit focused on real-world assets and infrastructure, the MEX launchpad and DAOaaS brought the community side of Web3 into the conversation.

events.title: Monster GameFi Soft Launch
events.description: I hosted the Monster GameFi soft launch in Bali during Coinfest week, a community event run by ASEAN Labs in joint venture with HODL, Kripto101, Pionex and 9Bit. The launch introduced the partners’ new products to the community, and it was equally a chance to network with Bali’s Web3 communities. Four partners joined ASEAN Labs to make it happen, and it was a pleasure to host it.
events.conclusion: The Monster GameFi soft launch put four partners behind one community event and gave their new products direct access to Bali’s Web3 communities during Coinfest week.

events.title: Chain of Trust
events.description: I presented ASEAN Labs at Chain of Trust, an event hosted by CCACC and Fableration for Malaysia’s Web3 and tech communities. ASEAN Labs is a Web3 project incubator that helps teams build on ENI across Southeast Asia, and my talk introduced it together with the ecosystem of projects we have incubated. The programme also included lucky draws and giveaways in stablecoins and project tokens. Thanks to CCACC and Fableration for having us.
events.conclusion: Chain of Trust brought the ASEAN Labs ecosystem to Malaysia’s Web3 and tech communities in person, a reminder that trust is built face to face and that giveaways only open the door.

events.title: Christmas Crypto Gala
events.description: I joined the panel at the Christmas Crypto Gala, co-hosted by ASEAN Labs and MySekolahKripto, on the future of Web3 in Malaysia. The gala combined a project introduction session with the panel, whose speakers came from fintech, GameFi and PayFi, together with a representative from MDEC who joined in a personal capacity. It made for a good session to brainstorm and share ideas about where Web3 in Malaysia goes next.
events.conclusion: With fintech, GameFi, PayFi and MDEC voices on one panel, the Gala made clear that the future of Web3 in Malaysia is a conversation across sectors, and that open sessions for sharing ideas are where it moves forward.

events.title: PayGo × ENI Community Night
events.description: I presented ASEAN Labs at PayGo × ENI Community Night, hosted by PayGo and ASEAN Labs in joint venture with Finweek KL. The audience was diverse, with people from tech, fintech and Web3, and even college students. My session covered ASEAN Labs, what we offer and our portfolio, and we then discussed the Web3 industry in Malaysia, its challenges and the solutions. PayGo is an x402 payment gateway on ENI Mainnet, which made it a natural co-host for an ENI community night.
events.conclusion: Bringing tech, fintech, Web3 and college students into one room pointed to one conclusion: Web3 in Malaysia moves forward when its challenges and solutions are discussed openly across industries, not only among insiders.

events.title: NOVA × MEXC Builders Session
events.description: I was invited, in a personal capacity, to share my experience in Web3 at a session hosted by MySekolahKripto in joint venture with MEXC. The audience was a mix of college students and working professionals, so I spoke about why Web3 is worth looking at as an industry, the skills it asks for, the job opportunities and more. Thank you to MySekolahKripto and MEXC for the invitation, and to everyone who came to listen.
events.conclusion: Speaking from personal experience to students and working professionals, the session came down to the practical questions for anyone entering Web3: why the industry matters, which skills it needs and what jobs it offers.

events.title: Blockchain Evolution 2025
events.description: I represented GameSpace at Blockchain Evolution 2025, hosted by MySekolahKripto in joint venture with two GameFi projects, EUFT and GameSpace. I introduced the project and shared insights on GameFi with a public audience. To make GameFi something people could try, the session also ran mini games, giveaways and a mini tournament. Thank you to MySekolahKripto and EUFT for partnering with us.
events.conclusion: For GameSpace, the session was a reminder that GameFi is best introduced through play, with the mini games, giveaways and tournament letting the public experience the project rather than only hear about it.

apps.title: NARO
apps.description: NARO is an AI-driven on-chain asset launchpad on BNB Smart Chain, created by UXUY and Radar DAO. This is the prototype version, built on BNB Testnet. I built the frontend mobile-first with breakpoints scaling up to desktop, covering the primary views: Swap, Mining, Data, Me and My Team. It connects to testnet wallets, and includes a test data mode for previewing every screen.

story.label: The problem
story.text: An app already live, redesigned. The original NARO app is already live on BSC. I redesigned it mobile first, with breakpoints scaling up to a desktop version.

story.label: The idea
story.text: A prototype on BNB Testnet. The first version is an MVP and prototype on BNB Testnet, with demo data and test transactions. It covers the primary views of the app: Swap, Mining, Data, Me and My Team. It connects to testnet wallets, and a test data mode lets every screen be previewed.

story.label: Why this look
story.text: Near-black with one mint accent. The theme and brand assets came from the client's team: a near-black ground with one mint-green accent, the convention of trading products, where numbers need contrast and green reads as go. My part was carrying it into a layout built for the phone first, with Connect Wallet as the clear primary action and a visible BNB Testnet chip that marks the prototype as a prototype. On desktop the six destinations (Home, Swap, Mining, Data, Me and My Team) sit in a left rail.

story.label: How it was built
story.text: Flows mapped, then built with AI. I mapped out the prototype flows, then used AI to execute the code and the BNB Testnet integration. After iterating on the interactions and test states, I handed over the build.
